models.model: The king gives the book to the man. Cyning is nominative, męnn dative singular, and bōc accusative singular.
models.target: Keep agent, recipient and object distinct.
models.essential_meaning: Keep agent, recipient and object distinct.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not interpret męnn as plural merely because the spelling is also a plural form.

models.model: Hīe refers to the feminine singular book and is accusative object of rǣdde.
models.target: Resolve the inanimate feminine pronoun from agreement and syntax.
models.essential_meaning: Resolve the inanimate feminine pronoun from agreement and syntax.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not force hīe to mean they or a female person.

models.model: Either the king or the man can be meant. Both are masculine singular; morphology and the supplied context do not settle which is the reader.
models.target: Recognize genuine ambiguity rather than applying a nearest-noun rule.
models.essential_meaning: Recognize genuine ambiguity rather than applying a nearest-noun rule.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not treat the nearest preceding person as a grammatical requirement.

models.model: Se mann hīe rǣdde.

models.model: Truly, when the king’s daughter saw that Apollonius was so well trained in all excellent accomplishments, her heart fell in love with him. Then, after the end of the drinking feast, the maiden said to the king: “Dear father, a little while ago you allowed me to give Apollonius whatever I wished from your treasury.”
models.target: Preserve seeing and education, her reaction, the time phrase, permission, donor, recipient, free choice and the source of the gift.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve seeing and education, her reaction, the time phrase, permission, donor, recipient, free choice and the source of the gift.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not make Apollonius love the daughter or turn the earlier permission into a new command.

models.model: King Arcestrates said to her: “Give him whatever you wish.” Then she went out very happily and said: “Master Apollonius, with my father’s permission I give you two hundred pounds of gold and four hundred pounds’ weight of silver, and the greatest part of costly clothing, and twenty slave men.” And then she spoke thus to the slave men: “Carry with you these things which I promised Apollonius, my teacher, and place them inside the chamber before my friends.” This was then done in this way, according to the princess’s command; and all the men who saw them praised her gifts.
models.target: Preserve every gift, quantity, material, permission, instruction, promise and narrated result, including the relative clause’s actual antecedent.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve every gift, quantity, material, permission, instruction, promise and narrated result, including the relative clause’s actual antecedent.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not omit the servants, merge the two weight phrases, or make the gifts the subject of gesāwon.

models.model: Then indeed the banquet ended, and all the men arose, greeted the king and the princess, wished them well and went home. Apollonius also said: “You good king, who has compassion on the poor, and you princess, lover of learning, farewell!” He also looked toward the slave men whom the maiden had given him and said to them: “Take with you these things which the princess gave me, and let us go and seek our guesthouse so that we may rest.”
models.target: Preserve the two departures or intended movements, the addressees of each speech, the prior gift and the final purpose.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the two departures or intended movements, the addressees of each speech, the prior gift and the final purpose.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not replace the proposed journey by a narrated arrival or make the servant-directed commands address the king.

models.model: Hiere is the daughter as possessor of mōd; his refers to Apollonius in the expression for love toward him. The whole expression means that she fell in love with him.
models.target: Keep the two possessors and the direction of affection distinct, applying the supplied expression.
models.essential_meaning: Keep the two possessors and the direction of affection distinct, applying the supplied expression.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not interpret his as the daughter’s own love or infer an unexpressed change of subject.

models.model: The princess is ic, the giver; Apollonius is ðē, the dative recipient of giefan.
models.target: Recover person and dative recipient within direct speech.
models.essential_meaning: Recover person and dative recipient within direct speech.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not preserve the earlier king as the speaker of this new quotation.

models.model: The first is singular Apollonius, recipient of the slave men whom the maiden had given him. The second is plural, the slave men addressed by Apollonius. Context and clause roles resolve identical dative spellings.
models.target: Resolve two syncretic pronouns by clause roles and discourse.
models.essential_meaning: Resolve two syncretic pronouns by clause roles and discourse.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not assign both forms the same referent solely because they have the same spelling.

models.model: Geseah has the king’s daughter as subject; gefēoll has hiere mōd as grammatical subject. The meaning of the latter supplied expression is that she fell in love.
models.target: Separate literal grammatical subject from an idiomatic English rendering.
models.essential_meaning: Separate literal grammatical subject from an idiomatic English rendering.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not make hiere alone the nominative subject of gefēoll.

models.model: Punda is genitive plural of the counted weight-unit after twā hund; goldes is genitive singular naming the material measured. The complete supplied phrase means two hundred pounds of gold.
models.target: Apply the visible quantity analysis and distinguish counted units from material.
models.essential_meaning: Apply the visible quantity analysis and distinguish counted units from material.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not infer that both genitives have the same semantic dependency or introduce an independent high-numeral recall test.

models.model: The relative refers back to męnn despite intervening words; it represents the men as subject of gesāwon. Hīe is accusative plural, the gifts as object of seeing. Giefa is accusative plural, the gifts praised, with hiere as possessor.
models.target: Explain separation of antecedent and relative and distinguish subject from object with the source note visible.
models.essential_meaning: Explain separation of antecedent and relative and distinguish subject from object with the source note visible.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: The note already supplies the antecedent; the task asks how the complete structure works.

models.model: In 176.16 gesunde is accusative plural, agreeing with the infinitival subject hīe, the king and princess. In 176.18 it is nominative plural, agreeing with gē in the direct subjunctive wish. The identical surfaces participate in different clause structures; both expressions wish the addressees well or bid them farewell.
models.target: Apply the supplied farewell expressions and distinguish accusative plural from nominative plural predicate agreement.
models.essential_meaning: Apply the supplied farewell expressions and distinguish accusative plural from nominative plural predicate agreement.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not make gesunde an adverb merely because idiomatic English uses well.

models.model: Mid-ðȳ-ðe introduces the temporal frame with the daughter as perceiver; ðæt introduces the content of what she sees, Apollonius’s education; ðā introduces the ensuing main event, her falling in love.
models.target: Distinguish temporal subordination, embedded content and the main event.
models.essential_meaning: Distinguish temporal subordination, embedded content and the main event.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not label every subordinate clause a relative or flatten the three relations into coordination.

models.model: The first is the supplied permission-content construction. Swā-hwæt-swā introduces the freely chosen thing she may give; its object role is internal to the free-choice clause.
models.target: Apply the visibly supplied permission frame and prior free-choice analysis without treating their introductory forms as interchangeable.
models.essential_meaning: Apply the visibly supplied permission frame and prior free-choice analysis without treating their introductory forms as interchangeable.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not interpret swā-hwæt-swā as a direct question.

models.model: The final clause gives the purpose of the proposed journey to the guesthouse: so that they can rest. Gān wē is the locally supplied first-person plural exhortation, with sēcean; the goal is prospective.
models.target: Distinguish a proposal, its infinitival action and its purpose.
models.essential_meaning: Distinguish a proposal, its infinitival action and its purpose.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not treat the purpose as an accomplished event or infer a general future-tense auxiliary.

models.model: She invokes the king’s earlier permission; he renews permission to give whatever she wishes. She herself announces the particular gifts.
models.target: Distinguish authorization from the selection and announcement of gifts.
models.essential_meaning: Distinguish authorization from the selection and announcement of gifts.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not attribute each specified gift directly to a royal command.

models.model: He instructs the slave men to take the gifts and proposes going to their guesthouse to rest. This excerpt does not narrate their arrival or sleeping.
models.target: Separate intended action from completed narrative and respect the selected boundary.
models.essential_meaning: Separate intended action from completed narrative and respect the selected boundary.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible variants preserving every stated relation and the explicit target.
models.error_diagnosis: Do not import the following Apollonius as Teacher episode into the answer.
